topic.title: JavaScript DOM Manipulation
topic.description: Core DOM skills: selecting elements, changing content/styles, handling events and creating new elements dynamically. Built as a tiny todo-list so every technique is used in a real way.

learningNotes.whatILearned: One listener on the parent can handle every item, so a list of a thousand rows costs one handler instead of a thousand.
learningNotes.challenges: I left `markAllDone` defined but never called, and I add a class and then immediately remove it without saying why.
learningNotes.nextSteps: Call `markAllDone` from somewhere real or delete it, and say in a comment that the add-then-toggle pair is meant to cancel out.

misconceptions: `textContent` and `innerHTML` are not interchangeable — one sets text, the other parses markup, and only one of them is safe for user input
A listener on the container is not the same as a listener on every item — `event.target.closest()` is what makes the difference
`classList.toggle()` on a class that is already there removes it — that is why the first item is not marked done at the end
engine.review:
**The rubric I used**

There is no task sheet for this one — it was written before the engine
existed and it was never in the catalogue, so there was nothing to grade it
against. I graded the file on the three things that have always mattered
here:

- **40 — it runs.** It compiles or interprets without an error.
- **30 — it is right.** The output is what it claims to produce.
- **30 — it explains itself.** Comments say *why*, not *what*.

**40 + 28 + 28 = 96%**

**What is solid**

I could not run this in node — `document` does not exist there — so I ran it
under a real DOM instead. It works: the heading is created and appended, the
three demo tasks land in the list, the button and the input are wired, and
the first item ends up *not* marked done.

That last one is the interesting part. You add `done` and then toggle it, so
it is gone again. That is not a bug — it is the demonstration — but you do
not say so anywhere, and I had to work it out.

**Fix this first**

Two small things, and neither is wrong:

- `markAllDone()` is defined and never called. Either call it from the
  button, or delete it. Dead code in a teaching file is worse than no code,
  because the reader assumes it was left in on purpose.
- `classList.add("done")` immediately followed by `classList.toggle("done")`
  looks like a mistake. One line of comment — *the toggle removes it again;
  that is the point* — turns it into the lesson it was meant to be.

**Then this**

Your comments are already the good kind. The event-delegation one is
genuinely excellent: *ONE listener on the parent handles every item. Far
better than attaching hundreds of listeners.* That is a why, and it is the
reason the whole pattern exists.

The `innerHTML` warning is the same: *only for trusted HTML!* — that is a
security note attached to the exact line where it applies.

**One thing to re-read**

The closing block, *Key takeaways I keep in mind*. Five lines, each one a
rule you would actually want to remember. That is the part of this file
worth copying into whatever you write next.
